about: A real `datamend watch airflow` agent run on the signups_daily failure in the local datamend-airflow-demo repo (Airflow 3.3.2), recorded for replay in tests and demos. Its trajectory was captured live from the agent's event stream.

content.text: {"root_cause": "The vendor feed (commit 252ba5f) now includes signup_date values in DD/MM/YYYY format (ids 37, 39, 40: '23/10/2026', '24/10/2026', '05/10/2026'). parse_row in dags/signups.py only called date.fromisoformat, which accepts only YYYY-MM-DD. It raised ValueError on the first slash-formatted row, so the whole load_signups task failed.", "fix": "In dags/signups.py I added parse_date(). It parses values containing '/' with strptime('%d/%m/%Y') and passes everything else to date.fromisoformat. parse_row now calls it. I also imported datetime. The output table schema is unchanged: signup_id INTEGER, email VARCHAR, signup_date DATE, plan VARCHAR. No records are dropped or altered apart from the date parsing. A date in any other unrecognised format still raises a ValueError instead of being skipped or zeroed.", "rationale": "The failure comes from the parser not handling a new input format, so the fix is to make the parser handle it. Skipping the bad rows would silently lose valid signups, and the contract doesn't allow that. Replacing the bad dates with NULL would do the same. Treating '/' dates as DD/MM/YYYY matches the vendor's commit message, and values like 23/10 and 24/10 can't be MM/DD. Unknown formats still fail loudly so a further feed change gets noticed. I couldn't run the code or add tests, so I changed only the parser.", "risk": "The DD/MM reading of '05/10/2026' (id 40) is inferred. It is ambiguous on its own and would be wrong if the vendor mixes MM/DD with DD/MM. If the vendor switches to a different format, the task will fail again, deliberately. I didn't add a test or a quarantine path for unparseable rows. If the data contract allows quarantining, that would be a better long-term handling. The vendor should be asked to confirm the date format or go back to ISO dates.", "confidence": 0.85}
